product_brief: A CoreDNS plugin integrating post-quantum cryptographic algorithms to enable quantum-resistant DNSSEC functionality.
pqc_capability_description: The implementation is a plugin for CoreDNS that extends it with support for five PQC signature algorithm families: ML-DSA, FALCON, SPHINCS+, MAYO, and SNOVA. It provides on-the-fly signing using quantum-resistant signatures while maintaining compatibility with existing DNS resolution flows. Performance evaluation reveals trade-offs between security and efficiency.
crypto_primitives: RSA, ECDSA, ED25519, ML-DSA, FALCON, SPHINCS+, MAYO, SNOVA
pqc_roadmap_details: The paper describes the integration of standard and candidate algorithms (FALCON, ML-DSA, SPHINCS+, MAYO, SNOVA) into CoreDNS to provide empirical performance data for algorithm selection and deployment planning in containerized DNS environments.
signature_schemes: RSA, ECDSA, ED25519, ML-DSA, FALCON, SPHINCS+, MAYO, SNOVA
testing_&_validation_methods: Benchmarking and performance evaluation were performed to reveal trade-offs between security and efficiency.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: The implementation maintains compatibility with existing DNS resolution flows. Challenges include increased signature and key sizes (10-50 times larger), impacting UDP transmission and potentially forcing TCP transport, which introduces latency.

product_brief: DNS software platform modified to support Post-Quantum Cryptography algorithms for DNSSEC signing and validation.
pqc_capability_description: PowerDNS was modified to support PQC algorithms Falcon, Dilithium, SPHINCS+, XMSS, and XMSSMT for DNSSEC. Implementation uses liboqs and OpenSSL 3 provider (oqs-provider). Testing involved deploying zones signed with these algorithms and measuring deliverability. Validation support implemented in PowerDNS Recursor.
crypto_primitives: RSASHA256, Falcon, Dilithium, SPHINCS+, XMSS, XMSSMT
signature_schemes: RSASHA256, Falcon, Dilithium, SPHINCS+, XMSS, XMSSMT
testing_&_validation_methods: Interoperability testing between PowerDNS and BIND; field study using RIPE ATLAS network to measure response delivery rates and correctness.

product_brief: DNS security utilities and library providing DNSSEC signing, verification, and resolution tools.
pqc_capability_description: The document does not mention Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms, support, or migration plans. It focuses on classical DNSSEC algorithms and standard cryptographic libraries like OpenSSL.
crypto_primitives: Ed25519, Ed448, DSA, RSA (implied by OpenSSL support and standard DNSSEC context, though only Ed25519/Ed448/DSA explicitly named in changelog features), OpenSSL
primary_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, Solaris, Cygwin, BSDs, musl libc, tvOS
implementation_attack_surface: Memory leaks, null pointer dereferences, heap out-of-bound reads, assertion failures, timing-sensitive TSIG compare vulnerability, potential NULL dereferences, free after reallocing to 0 size.
testing_&_validation_methods: Unit tests, coverity static analysis, shellcheck, CI testing (Cygwin, BSDs, musl libc, 32-bit, big-endian), fuzzing (implied by security fixes from external reporters like pokerfacett).
deployment_&_migration_complexity: API changes noted (e.g., ldns_dnssec_*_add_rr() return value change in 1.9.0), soname version bumps, breaking changes in Python bindings.
